findings.problem: The chance bars of rows 1 in 8 and 1 in 16 are drawn the same width (42 px) although the data says 37.5 px and 18.75 px. A7.bar is a .v-card (box-sizing border-box, 3 px border) with a fixed padding of 0 18px, so it can never be narrower than 42 px. The storyboard's whole point ('the fill of row 4 is 18.75 px wide: rare = tiny sliver') is lost: on the last beat the bar does not halve at all (42 -> 42), and rows 3 and 4 look identical. Scene 6 already hit this and fixes it locally ('b.el.style.padding = "0"'); scene 3 does not.
findings.fix: Give the bars in scene 3 no padding (they carry no text): after creating them, set track.el.style.padding = '0' and fill.el.style.padding = '0' (same line scene 6 uses), or better fix A7.bar once in common-2.js so padding is only applied when text is placed inside (padding: text && !textOut ? '0 18px' : '0') and drop the scene-6 workaround. Then row widths must read 300 / 150 / 75 / 37.5 / 18.75 px (a 14 px minimum is still enforced by the helper, so row 4 stays visible). Re-check with getBoundingClientRect on the blue .v-card elements at s3@10.
findings.evidence: Measured with Playwright at absolute 24 s (s3@10): blue fill widths 300, 150, 75, 42, 42 (style.width 37.5px and 18.8px, rendered 42 px). Stills s3@9 and s3@10.9: rows '1 in 8' and '1 in 16' have identical blue fills (x 242-284). Scene 6 comment: 'the helper's 18 px padding would keep every short bar at 42 px'.

findings.problem: Breaks the 12 px stage margin rule: the five row labels ('certain', '1 in 2', ... '1 in 16') sit at stage x = 0 (flush with the stage edge, 0 px margin) and the 'chance' / 'surprise' column header tags sit at y = 6 (6 px from the top). Every other scene keeps at least 12 px (measured minimum across scenes 2-10 is 11.6 to 40 px, only scene 3 is at 0 and 6). Also the key row ('1 bit = one yes-or-no answer') ends up only 12 px under the last row's lip, which makes the bottom of the ladder cramped.
findings.fix: Shift the ladder right by 12 px (labels x 12, bars x 182, cells x 552, tags x 752: the right edge still has 60 px spare), set the header tags to y 12, and reduce the row pitch from 108 to 104 (rowY = 80 + 104 k) so the key can move to about KEY_Y 574 and keep a 12 px gap above it and more than 12 px to the stage bottom.
findings.evidence: DOM scan of all stage elements at 0.2 s steps: scene 3 min left margin 0 ('1 in 16' tag, also certain/1 in 2/1 in 4/1 in 8), min top margin 6 ('surprise' tag at s3@0.5). Stills s3@5.9 and s3@9: labels touch the stage's left edge (x = 72 on the page), key row y 845-887 against the row-4 lip at about 830.

findings.problem: Maths symbols are typed as text glyphs in two tags although the storyboard says symbols (ticks, crosses, plus, equals) are SVG, never glyphs: scene 3's key reads '1 bit = one yes-or-no answer' (a glyph '='), and scene 4's tag reads '14 bits / 8 symbols' (a glyph '/'; the '=' next to the counter in the same scene is correctly an SVG A7.sym).
findings.fix: Scene 3: change the text to '1 bit: one yes-or-no answer' (the tick and cross beside it already carry the idea) or draw A7.sym('equals', ...) between the tick/cross and the words. Scene 4: write the tag as '14 bits for 8 symbols' (or '14 bits over 8 symbols'), which also reads better aloud.
findings.evidence: scene-03-surprise.js line 81: text: `${bitsText(LAD[1].bits)} = one yes-or-no answer`; scene-04-entropy.js line 97: text: `${S.total} bits / ${S.msg.length} symbols`. Stills s3@9 (bottom key tag) and s4@11.9 (tag right of the entropy counter).

findings.problem: A first-time learner never sees why a code is SENT: the lookup is only drawn when it succeeds (a blue ring on the matching dictionary chip, steps 2, 4, 5, 7). For the new-phrase steps 0, 1, 3 and 6 the caption says 'A new longer phrase: send a code, learn it.' but on screen there is only phrase 'A' and the orange ring on 'B' with no chip for 'AB' to be missing from, so 'new' has to be taken on trust. Scene 9 solves the same problem with a dashed '?' ghost chip.
findings.fix: During the ASK phase of an emit step, show a dashed ghost chip in the next free dictionary slot reading the phrase w + c (for example '2 | AB' dashed, orange ring, text in the -ink shade) with a short red cross (L5.cross) or the word 'not found' next to it; on ACT it fills in and becomes the orange new chip (so the learned entry visibly grows out of the miss). Keep it SVG/tag based and 28 px or more; the dictionary never loses a chip.
findings.evidence: Stills s8@3 (step 0 ask: only A, ringed B, dictionary 0 A / 1 B, no sign that AB is missing) versus s8@6 and s8@7.7 (known steps: blue ring on chip 2 AB = the only visible lookup). Caption [2.6-4.8] in scene-08-lzw-encode.js.

findings.problem: The last caption 'Nine letters became five codes.' fades in at 11.4 s while the fifth code is still flying: the '3' tile reaches its slot at about 11.6 s and the '9 letters, 5 codes' tag pops at 11.9 s, so the caption runs about 0.2 to 0.5 s ahead of its picture (house rule: a caption never runs ahead of the picture).
findings.fix: Start the caption at 11.9 (caps [11.9, 12.9, ...]); the tag is then already popping.
findings.evidence: Stills s8@11.2 (code 3 still on the blue/green bracket, only 0 1 2 4 in the sent row, no caption), s8@11.5 (3 mid-flight at x 655, caption fading in), s8@11.7 (landed, tag visible).

findings.problem: Vocabulary mismatch: the caption says 'Each code adds one entry to the table.' but the on-screen label (and scene 8) calls it the dictionary, which is the only word defined on screen. 'table' is an undefined second name for the same thing.
findings.fix: Change the caption to 'Each code adds one entry to the dictionary.' (it still fits on one line at 40 px).
findings.evidence: scene-09-lzw-decode.js caps [4.7, 6.3]; still s9@5.5 shows the purple 'dictionary' tag above the chips and the caption below it saying 'table'.
